[ASSISTANT_SAID] Get regular exercise: Regular aerobic exercise helps improve sleep quality, reduce stress, and increase overall well-being.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Practice relaxation techniques: Incorporate relaxation techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, and yoga into your routine to reduce stress and promote a good night's sleep.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Avoid caffeine and alcohol: Avoid drinking caffeine or alcohol before bedtime as they can disrupt sleep quality.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Set boundaries for electronics use: Limit your screen time each day and set rules for when and where you can use electronic devices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Consider a tech-free hour before bedtime: Establish an hour of the day when all electronics must be turned off, allowing your body to relax and prepare for sleep.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Read or listen to calming music: Try listening to calming music or read a relaxing book before bedtime to help you wind down.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Seek medical advice: If you continue to struggle with sleep, talk to your doctor or a sleep specialist. They can help you identify any underlying causes and develop a treatment plan.
